title: New vowel, new word
goal: Blend a CVC word with a newly taught vowel and read it in a controlled sentence.
evidence: Listen for /d/ /o/ /g/ blended as dog and accurate reading of the sentence; note audio support.
lesson: After explicit teaching of short o; transfer to dot or got on paper.

title: Two letters, one sound
goal: Read sh as one sound and blend it with other taught correspondences.
evidence: Student blends shop without separating s and h, then reads Sam sat in a shop.; check a different sh word.
lesson: After teaching sh; use ship as the next independent word.

title: Keep every sound
goal: Blend an initial consonant cluster without omitting either consonant.
evidence: Teacher hears all five phonemes in stamp, accurate stamps in the sentence and transfer to another taught cluster word.
lesson: Consolidation when individual correspondences are secure; contrast stamp with another cluster word orally.

title: The shrinking puddle
goal: Explain evaporation and predict how shade could affect a puddle under otherwise similar conditions.
evidence: Diagram and narration link liquid water to water vapour in air; prediction has a reason and recognises other conditions.
lesson: After observing puddles or modelling changes of state; discuss what the diagram cannot show.

title: Change the pivot
goal: Use a lever model to explain how pivot position affects the effort required for the same load.
evidence: Student relates distances from the pivot to the load and effort and provides a consistent diagram/narration.
lesson: Consolidation after a physical lever demonstration; predict before testing.

title: A change in a food chain
goal: Explain a possible indirect effect in a simple food-chain model and state an assumption.
evidence: Narration connects fewer caterpillars to their food and predators; student explains uncertainty rather than claiming certainty.
lesson: After teaching food-chain arrow meaning; compare the simplified chain with an actual habitat.

title: Shade or a smoother path?
goal: Recommend a council project within a budget while addressing competing access and comfort needs.
evidence: Choice cites both resident views, calculates remaining funds and acknowledges a trade-off.
lesson: Apply agreed decision criteria after learning about local services.

title: A weekend street market
goal: Compare two public-space proposals using cost, access and competing community interests.
evidence: Student uses a cost and both perspectives to justify a choice and proposes a mitigation.
lesson: Small-group deliberation before an individual council statement.

title: A service beyond the trial
goal: Distinguish a funded trial from an ongoing commitment and justify a decision under uncertainty.
evidence: Student cites trial costs, access needs and unknown future funding; identifies information needed.
lesson: Later civics lesson on recurring costs and evaluating proposals.

title: Weather at one spot
goal: Record a temperature comparison with consistent method and separate measured change from explanation.
evidence: Student uses units, time and location, identifies a measured difference and proposes a further observation.
lesson: Outdoor weather mission followed by a short classroom comparison.

title: A puddle after rain
goal: Use repeated observations of one location to describe change while recognising limits of the measurement.
evidence: Student distinguishes a shorter puddle from a measured volume loss and proposes a way to improve evidence.
lesson: After rainfall observation; revisit safely with teacher and compare class records.

title: An unfamiliar leaf
goal: Describe observable features before offering an uncertain identification.
evidence: Record uses visible shape, edge and arrangement, keeps identification tentative and names evidence needed.
lesson: School-ground observation station; compare records before using a teacher-approved field guide.

title: More individuals or more groups?
goal: Distinguish abundance from the number of observed organism groups using comparable samples.
evidence: Student compares totals and represented groups, and avoids treating broad groups as species counts.
lesson: Classroom analysis following consistent garden and mulch sampling.

title: Repeat the sample
goal: Use repeated counts to describe variation and avoid relying on one sample.
evidence: Student cites all three paired samples, identifies the overall pattern and gives a limitation.
lesson: After field sampling; teach how repeats strengthen comparison without proving a cause.

title: Can these counts be compared?
goal: Identify unequal sampling effort and redesign a fairer habitat comparison.
evidence: Student spots area and duration differences and specifies a common repeat method before drawing conclusions.
lesson: Use as a diagnostic task before the next outdoor investigation.

title: Surface and stopping distance
goal: Identify the changed variable and justify a conclusion using controlled simulation results.
evidence: Student compares distances, names surface as changed variable and proposes a useful repeat or extension.
lesson: Virtual investigation after explicitly modelling fair tests.

title: Keeping water warm
goal: Interpret controlled cooling data and distinguish evidence from a general claim about materials.
evidence: Student uses the temperature change or final temperatures, identifies controlled conditions and suggests repeats.
lesson: After predicting which wrapping will reduce cooling; compare with a supervised physical test if suitable.

title: Plan a dissolving test
goal: Design a fair test by changing water temperature while controlling relevant quantities and method.
evidence: Student specifies temperature as independent variable, consistent sugar/water/stirring and a measurable end point.
lesson: Planning phase before simulation; discuss predictions before running.

title: A smaller batch
goal: Halve every ingredient in a recipe while preserving proportions.
evidence: Student halves all three quantities consistently and explains the operation.
lesson: After physical halving; check the same reasoning with a different recipe.

title: Share the muffins
goal: Represent equal sharing and explain the link between total, groups and group size.
evidence: Student distributes 12 muffins among 4 plates equally and explains how they know shares are equal.
lesson: Small-group division task; repeat with counters off screen.

title: A recipe for six
goal: Scale ingredient quantities by a factor of three and justify the multiplicative relationship.
evidence: Student triples both quantities rather than adding the same number to each.
lesson: Year 3–4 recipe scaling after equal-groups modelling.

title: Read the scale
goal: Read a volume from equally spaced graduations and explain the reading.
evidence: Student identifies 300 mL using the scale and describes the marked interval; audio/text evidence.
lesson: Measurement rotation before using real calibrated containers.

title: Use equal measures
goal: Connect repeated equal measures to a target volume and explain the calculation.
evidence: Student calculates four 250 mL measures for 1 L and checks the unit relationship.
lesson: After modelling 1 L = 1000 mL with containers.

title: Share a litre
goal: Find equal portions of a given volume and explain a division strategy.
evidence: Student calculates 250 mL each for four equal portions and shows the total is conserved.
lesson: Application after equal sharing with physical water or counters.

title: The fallen tower
goal: Retell a pictured event with a clear beginning, change and resolution.
evidence: Recording identifies people, event order and a reason connecting the problem to response; revision improves one unclear point.
lesson: Oral language small group after teacher models sequencing words.

title: A lunchbox mix-up
goal: Describe people and objects precisely enough for a listener to follow a story.
evidence: Student distinguishes two similar objects using relevant detail and clarifies ambiguous pronouns.
lesson: EAL/D or oral-language lesson on description and reference.

title: The windy picnic
goal: Explain causal connections in an oral narrative and consider a plausible ending.
evidence: Student uses because/so meaningfully, keeps events coherent and improves clarity after playback.
lesson: Lesson on connecting events rather than simply listing pictures.

title: A seed story
goal: Organise a picture sequence and retell it with clear time language.
evidence: Recording links planting, watering and later growth with appropriate sequence terms.
lesson: Speaking and listening lesson after a simple class planting experience.

title: Explain a classroom routine
goal: Give a clear oral explanation of a familiar sequence for a new classmate.
evidence: Listener can identify necessary steps and their order; revised recording fills a missing step.
lesson: Speaking lesson on audience awareness; test by asking a partner to retell the routine.

title: One picture, different stories
goal: Develop a coherent oral narrative while distinguishing visible detail from imagined events.
evidence: Student describes the shared picture, supplies a coherent own story and revises for listener clarity; different stories are acceptable.
lesson: Pair storytelling task comparing two interpretations of the same image.

title: Map the reading room
goal: Use a key and grid references to locate landmarks and create directions another person can follow.
evidence: Partner follows directions from A3 to C1, with landmarks named consistently; student revises ambiguity.
lesson: After walking a school room and discussing bird’s-eye maps.

title: A playground route
goal: Use cardinal directions and landmarks to communicate a route on a map.
evidence: Student describes a route from gate to fountain that avoids a closed square; partner test verifies route.
lesson: Geography route planning after a school-ground walk.

title: Choose useful map symbols
goal: Create a consistent map key and use it to explain the location of a landmark.
evidence: Student matches each symbol to one place and describes relative position using the map.
lesson: Map-making phase before exchanging navigation challenges.

title: A place to borrow books
goal: Compare candidate service locations by walking distance and justify a spatial decision.
evidence: Student counts orthogonal moves accurately and explains whose access improves or worsens.
lesson: Settlement planning task after teaching grid movement and scale.

title: A safe way to the oval
goal: Plan a route using a map constraint and estimate its distance from a simple scale.
evidence: Student avoids the closed square, counts five orthogonal moves from A3 to D1 and explains the detour.
lesson: Navigation challenge after reading a map key.

title: Two parks, different needs
goal: Use map distance and information about users to justify a location decision with trade-offs.
evidence: Student compares both sites from homes and school and explains why no site meets every need equally.
lesson: Group planning followed by an individual geographic justification.

title: The unopened invitation
goal: Infer a character’s possible motivation from textual clues without treating inference as fact.
evidence: Student cites the hidden invitation and question, explains a plausible motive and offers an alternative.
lesson: Guided comprehension discussion on character motives.

title: Before the rain
goal: Make a plausible prediction supported by more than one textual clue.
evidence: Prediction connects clouds and preparations, acknowledges that the future event is not certain.
lesson: Pause-before-reading-on activity in a comprehension lesson.

title: The missing class plant
goal: Reconcile apparently conflicting statements by considering sequence and limits of knowledge.
evidence: Student uses yesterday/today timing and the pot clue to propose a coherent explanation without accusing a character.
lesson: Later comprehension task on contradictions and revised inference.

title: Reading between the words
goal: Infer emotion from action and context while allowing more than one interpretation.
evidence: Student quotes observable actions, explains the inference and identifies another plausible interpretation.
lesson: Close-reading mini-lesson before independent inference practice.

title: A clue that changes the idea
goal: Revise an inference when a new clue weakens the first explanation.
evidence: Student identifies which evidence challenges the claim and gives a better-supported alternative.
lesson: Teacher-led think-aloud followed by individual revised inference.

title: Whose account fits?
goal: Compare two accounts against a third piece of textual evidence and explain uncertainty.
evidence: Student distinguishes statements from corroborating evidence and avoids claiming more than the text establishes.
lesson: Comprehension extension on differing viewpoints and evidence.

title: One glue stick
goal: Consider two people’s needs and compare possible ways to share a limited resource.
evidence: Student proposes a response, predicts effects for both children and discusses an alternative without a single correct score.
lesson: Teacher-guided role-play during a cooperative classroom activity.

title: A quiet place to work
goal: Explore how differing sensory and activity needs can be accommodated through discussion.
evidence: Student asks rather than assumes what each person needs, proposes an adjustment and considers both effects.
lesson: Class discussion before group work; adult supports any needed accommodation.

title: A change to the game
goal: Discuss fairness when rules change and propose a response that considers different perspectives.
evidence: Student explains both concerns, predicts consequences and revises a proposal after hearing another view.
lesson: Teacher-facilitated social problem-solving before playground role-play.

title: Name the destination
goal: Replace an ambiguous reference with a precise noun or location and verify the result.
evidence: Student specifies the intended red flag rather than an unclear it and explains how the change resolves ambiguity.
lesson: Procedural writing mini-lesson on precise references.

title: Put the steps in order
goal: Sequence procedural actions so that each required condition is met before the next action.
evidence: Student places pickup before delivery and describes why the original order cannot work.
lesson: Writing directions lesson; test a revised sequence with a partner.

title: Say when to stop
goal: Add a clear stopping condition to an instruction and explain how it prevents unintended movement.
evidence: Student names a visible stopping point before the bridge, tests it and revises if necessary.
lesson: Extension after precise action verbs and directions have been taught.

title: A precise description
goal: Revise vague wording with relevant detail drawn from the writer’s own notes.
evidence: Student adds informative detail, preserves the intended event and explains how it helps a reader.
lesson: Focused revision after drafting; teacher assigns description as the single goal.

title: Support an opinion
goal: Add a relevant supporting reason to an opinion using the writer’s intended idea.
evidence: Revision links opinion and reason, avoids unrelated detail and explains the reader benefit.
lesson: Persuasive-writing conference focusing on one reason.

title: Clarify who did what
goal: Resolve an ambiguous reference while preserving the writer’s intended meaning.
evidence: Student replaces or clarifies an unclear pronoun and explains how the reader can identify the actor.
lesson: Revision lesson on cohesion after students have drafted a short recount.
